The polar curves $r=5-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ and $r=1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ intersect  for $\theta \in [{0}^{∘},{360}^{∘})$ at points $A$ and $B,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates $({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})$ and $({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})$ of the points $A$ and $B,$ respectively? worked_solution:
To determine the polar coordinates of the intersection points, we will solve the following system of equations for $r$ and $\theta :$  

$$
\{\begin{aligned}r=5-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ r=1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

We begin by setting the equations equal to each other and solve for $\theta .$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =4 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation in the interval $[{0}^{∘},{360}^{∘}),$ we obtain ${\theta }_{1}={30}^{∘}$ and ${\theta }_{2}={150}^{∘}.$ 

Now, we use the equation $r=1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ to find the $r$-coordinates of the intersection points: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1} & =1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡{\theta }_{1}=1+4\cdot \frac{1}{2}=3 \\ {r}_{2} & =1+4\operatorname{sin}⁡{\theta }_{2}=1+4\cdot \frac{1}{2}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of the points of intersection are

$$
({r}_{A},{\theta }_{A})=(3,{30}^{∘})\,\text{and }({r}_{B},{\theta }_{B})=(3,{150}^{∘}).
$$
